headline: **MLB Daily Recap: August 13, 2026**
article:
The Detroit Tigers secured a shutout victory over the Cleveland Guardians, winning 3-0. Eduardo Valencia led the Guardians' offense with a home run and an RBI. In other action, the Cincinnati Reds edged the Chicago White Sox in a thrilling 9-8 victory, with Eugenio Suárez leading the Reds' offense with a home run and 4 RBIs. The Pittsburgh Pirates cruised to a dominant 13-1 victory over the Miami Marlins, with Rafael Flores Jr. recording 2 hits, 2 home runs, and 6 RBIs. The Seattle Mariners took down the New York Yankees in a low-scoring affair, 1-0, with Logan Gilbert earning the win. The Chicago Cubs secured a 3-0 shutout victory over the St. Louis Cardinals, with Seiya Suzuki having a notable performance.

Several players have been impacted by injuries and availability. Seattle Mariners shortstop Colt Emerson has been placed on the 10-day injured list due to left wrist tendon inflammation. The Chicago White Sox have placed right-hander Davis Martin on the 15-day injured list due to a right middle finger blister. The San Francisco Giants have transferred third baseman Matt Chapman from the 10-day injured list to the 60-day injured list due to an abdominal strain, and right-hander Trevor McDonald has been transferred from the 15-day injured list to the 60-day injured list with a right elbow strain. The Boston Red Sox have placed right-hander Garrett Whitlock on the 15-day injured list retroactive to August 10, 2026, due to right elbow inflammation. The Detroit Tigers have placed center fielder James Outman on the 7-day injured list with a concussion, and the Pittsburgh Pirates have placed catcher Endy Rodríguez on the 10-day injured list retroactive to August 10, 2026, due to left hip inflammation. The Toronto Blue Jays have placed right-hander Jake Bloss on the 60-day injured list.

There have been several trades and roster movements in the past 24 hours. The Boston Red Sox traded center fielder Harold Rivas to the Baltimore Orioles as part of the 8/3 Adley Rutschman trade. The Miami Marlins traded first baseman Jacob Berry to the Kansas City Royals.
